items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...There's King Oliver and Jelly Roll Morton... [INTERVIEWEE] That's right, yes.

ctx.x: So what could we possibly do? Anyway, that became a big hit, record-wise. And so, I guess people are still listening to it now and then.

Well, yes, they are. I mean, it's considered by the critical establishment in jazz one of the great duets ever recorded. There's King Oliver and Jelly Roll Morton. There's Louie Armstrong and Earl Hines. There's you and Don Byas and there's a couple others. But I mean, in the list of the great jazz duets, that's one of them that's always mentioned. It's never mentioned that they talk about the great duets in jazz that that's not one of them.
